# Draft:President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo Award of Outstanding Achievement

Background
The President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Award of Outstanding Achievement or President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Achievement Awards(PGMA-AA) were annual national recognitions of excellent and deserving students in the Philippines during the administration of former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo from 2003 to 2009. It was established by the Department of Education (DepEd) for high school and the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) for college.. It essentially aimed to honor outstanding achievements and academic excellence among graduating students in secondary and tertiary education in the Philippines.
Legal Framework
The PGMA-AA was initially launched through Department of Education (DepEd) Department Order No. 51, Series of 2003, titled "2003 President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Achievement Awards (PGMA-AA)" and  succeeded by the following DepEd Department Orders:
*Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 22, Series of 2004, titled "2004 - President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo (PGMA) Award of Outstanding Achievement" .
*Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 3, series of 2005, titled "The 2005 President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Award of Outstanding Achievement".
*Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 48, series of 2006, titled "President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo 2006 Academic Excellence and Leadership Award".
*Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 48, series of 2007, titled "2007 President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Outstanding Achievement and Academic Excellence Award".
*Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 69, series of 2008, titled "2008 President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Outstanding Achievements and Academic Excellence Awards".
*Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 19, series of 2009, titled "2009 President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Outstanding Achievements and Academic Excellence Awards".
*Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 91, series of 2010, titled "2010 President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Award of Outstanding Achievements and Academic Excellence Awards".
The conferment of the awards aimed to recognize deserving students and to further motivate them to strive for excellence beyond general academics and to recognize specialized talents that contribute to nation-building and community development.
The PGMA Award focused on "pockets of excellence" unlike the traditional "Valedictorian" or "Salutatorian" titles, which are based on general weighted averages across all subjects . It was typically presented during commencement exercises to one student per category in every public and private secondary school in the country.
Categories and Qualifications Per Year
During the early years (2003–2005) of its conferment  the President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Awards (PGMA-AA) were focused on five co-curricular categories, with one awardee per category per school:
*Student Leadership. This award was presented to students with active involvement as officers in school organizations (especially student council or government) and notable service to the school and community.
*Campus Journalism. This award is conferred  to students that exhibited outstanding achievements in school papers or campus organs who exemplified talent and professional ethics worthy to be emulated.
*Athletics. The recipient of this award is the most outstanding athlete who embodied genuine sportsmanship and brought pride to the school and community.
*Culture and Arts. A student who exhibited  excellence in visual, performing, or literary arts is the recipient of this award.
*Technology and Entrepreneurship. A student  who excelled in Technology and Livelihood Education, often through participation in skills competitions like STEP or YECS, is the recipient of this recognition.
In 2006, the President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Award for Outstanding Achievement consists of five categories of excellence namely: student leadership, campus journalism, athletics, culture and arts, and technology and entrepreneurship
In each category, there were five student to be chosen in both public and private school wherein the awards will be in the nature of an open competition focusing on total achievement notwithstanding the performance in academic work nor the year level of the student.
The awards were in the form of a customized medals (or medallions) bearing the engraved seal of the Philippine president and certificates or citations, also with the official seal of the President prominent in the design and with the signature of the President.
*A student who has shown active involvement in the school organizations as an officer particularly the student council and other clubs and organizations and have exhibited notable performance in implementing programs and projects in the delivering services for the school and the nearby community was the recipient of the 2006 President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo Award for outstanding achievement for student leadership.
*For the category of outstanding achievement award for campus journalism will be given to the student with the most outstanding achievement in the campus paper, other school organs and journals and who has exhibited the proper ethics, skills and talent in the various fields of journalism and has brought prestige and honor to their school through various competitions and exposures.
*The most outstanding athlete received the PGMA award for athletics, regardless of whatever sports combination, whether competitive or not, and who exemplifies the ideals of healthy and honorable sportsmanship and has brought pride and honor to their school.
*The PGMA award for culture was given to a student who has manifested excellence in the field of arts, whether it be in visual, performance and literary and has also brought honor and prestige to their school through competitions and other exposures.
*A student who excelled in the field of technology and livelihood education and has been an active participant in the Skills and Training Competition and has shown great potential in entrepreneurial endeavors was the recipient of the Technology and Entrepreneurship award.
The school principal and the department heads will select the five awardees, the names of which will be submitted to the division offices for consolidation and reporting.
In later years (2007-2010)  , the program expanded to include a specific category for overall academic performance alongside the original five co-curricular categories:
*Academic Excellence Award. The graduating Valedictorian of the school is the recipient of this award.
*Outstanding Achievement Awards. The award  continued the 2004–2005 blueprint of recognition for one student each that excelled in fields of Leadership, Journalism, Athletics, Culture and Arts, and Technology/Entrepreneurship.
The Awards
The selected students received a Presidential citation or certificate of recognition and a gold medal bearing the engraved Seal of the President of the Philippines.
Transition and Discontinuation
Following the end of term of President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo administration in 2010, the annual recognitions were scrapped and revised. Under the K-to-12 program implemented during the Presidency of Benigno Aquino III, the Department of Education (DepEd) issued new guidelines for awards and recognitions that standardized honors under different nomenclatures, such as "With Highest Honors, With High Honors, and With Honor"
